rule: Do not ingest company/banker TAM as target revenue without normalizing serviceable market, share, competition and reinvestment.
Do not select peers, metrics or forward periods to rationalize a desired market price.
Do not increase WACC arbitrarily because a company feels uncertain.
Do not forecast growth without the reinvestment needed to create it.
Do not let perpetual growth exceed sustainable economy/currency growth without an explicit override and warning.
Do not assume perpetual ROC far above WACC without durable competitive-advantage evidence.
Do not convert a company-specific target margin, market share, growth rate or sales-to-capital assumption into a universal sector rule.
Do not treat a dated benchmark spreadsheet as current without checking its as-of date.
Do not use non-operating assets as a balance-sheet catch-all or double count assets already in operating cash flows.
Do not force a peer set when economics are materially incomparable.
Do not weight source importance by document length or disclosure volume.
Do not change DCF value for a technical/index/sentiment event unless it changes cash-flow economics or systematic risk.
Do not learn from unexplained stale company names, dates or disconnected formulas inside a reused spreadsheet template.
